cohort_note: BOTM-RESEARCH-PORTO-SOURCES-01 / LISBON-PORTO-OVERNIGHT-COVERAGE-01 (2026-08-24): 19 credible Greater Porto leads researched in one bounded overnight session, following docs/SOURCE_REGISTRY.md's existing Lisbon conventions exactly (same schema, same three-field monitoring/lifecycle/rights model). Two entries (casa-da-musica, teatro-municipal-do-porto) were directly, technically proven live and are implemented by ingestion/lisbon-porto/run.mjs tonight. The rest are genuine research findings recorded honestly at whatever stage this session's bounded investigation actually reached — several are NEEDS_TECHNICAL_REVIEW because their public listing is rendered client-side by a JavaScript site-builder platform this project has no headless-browser collector family for (not attempted, not silently marked impossible). entries.name: Casa da Música
entries.acquisition_path_detail: LISBON-PORTO-OVERNIGHT-COVERAGE-01: proven live. The public /agenda/ listing server-renders one schema.org `itemscope itemtype="Event"` microdata card per session (12 observed live on page 1 of at least 11, `<link rel="next">` pagination confirmed), each carrying a genuine machine-readable `<time datetime="YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS">`, a first-party `/event/{slug}/?selected_session={id}` link embedding the site's own numeric WordPress 'session' custom-post-type id, a room/auditorium sub-location, a descriptive genre-like subtitle line, and (where priced) a €-price. Research also confirmed a wp-json/wp/v2/event and /session REST namespace exists (x-wp-total 1390) but no usable performance-date field was found there within this bounded proof, so the HTML listing's own <time> attributes are used instead. See ingestion/casa-da-musica/discovery.mjs and ingestion/casa-da-musica/observation-adapter.mjs.

Technical proof does not review or clear rights.

entries.name: Super Bock Arena — Pavilhão Rosa Mota
entries.physical_address: Rua de Dom Manuel II, 4050-346 Porto
entries.acquisition_path_detail: LISBON-PORTO-P1-SOURCE-AUTOMATION-01: proven live. This venue runs 'The Events Calendar' WordPress plugin's list view — every event is a `<div id="post-{id}" class="type-tribe_events post-{id} tribe-events-category-{slug}...">` block, carrying the plugin's own first-party genre/category taxonomy (pop-rock, musica-brasileira, musica-portuguesa, eletronica, fado, classica, forro, sertanejo, concertos-en, plus this venue's own genuinely non-music categories gaming/circo/stand-up-comedy/danca/infantil-2/musical), grouped under repeating month/year `<h2>` section headers. No `<link rel="next">` pagination was found live — a single fetch returns every currently-booked event, from 'now' through the venue's furthest booking (currently late 2027). Each card's own `tribe-event-date-start` text omits the year for a same-year event and includes it for a different-year one; this task's collector combines it with the card's own governing month-header text (never today's date) to derive a full calendar date. See ingestion/super-bock-arena/discovery.mjs and ingestion/super-bock-arena/observation-adapter.mjs.

entries.name: Hard Club
entries.physical_address: Praça do Infante D. Henrique, Porto
entries.acquisition_path_detail: A genuine first-party AJAX endpoint was directly found and fetched live: GET /include/ajax_functions.php?action=load-agenda&start=0&langid=1&passo=15 returns a real HTML fragment of dated event cards (real Sep-Dec 2026 titles observed). However, the fragment's own '.data' field carries only a day-of-month, never a month name — a per-event page's sidebar widget shows day+abbreviated-month for the 3 nearest events only, not the full listing — so this bounded proof could not establish an honest, unambiguous month for every card without risking a wrong-month fabrication. Not implemented tonight on that basis (per this task's 'never fabricate' rule), not because the endpoint itself is inaccessible. PORTO-COVERAGE-02 (2026-08-24) revisited this exact gap per that task's own explicit first priority, fetching the CURRENT site again in depth: the per-event detail page (/PT/evento/{slug}/) exposes NO schema.org/JSON-LD, no <time datetime> element, and no calendar/ICS link — its own visible content is the SAME day+abbreviated-month agenda widget, loaded via the same AJAX fragment (confirmed byte-identical shape). One genuinely NEW observation: the event permalink slug itself carries a trailing year suffix (e.g. '.../evento/johnny-hooker-euro-tour-2026-2026/') that DOES appear to track the real event year — walking the full ~22-event agenda in day-of-month order, the day sequence wraps around (28→01, 31→01 [the day-31 event is titled 'MOONSPELL INVICTA HALLOWEEN', corroborating an Oct 31 wrap], 21→29) exactly in step with the slug suffix flipping from '-2026' to '-2027' once. So the YEAR may be honestly derivable from the slug in sequence — but the MONTH remains fundamentally unresolvable: nothing on the listing or any per-event page states which calendar month a given day-of-month wrap actually lands in (a month could be entirely skipped between two listed events with no signal of that gap), and inferring it from wrap-position/sequence is exactly the 'never infer from sequence/order' prohibition this task itself sets. Still DEFERRED on that basis — this is a closer, better-understood near-miss than before, not a resolved source.

entries.name: Câmara Municipal do Porto — Open Data "Agenda Cultural"
entries.acquisition_path_detail: Technically excellent on paper: a CKAN open-data package (CC-Zero / public domain licence, machine-readable) exposing a single downloadable CSV resource (5.4MB, 1,087 rows: active/category/description/address/latitude/longitude/time/etc, sourced from https://city-api.wearebitmaker.com/CitySDK/events). Directly downloaded and inspected live. CONFIRMED STALE: every row's embedded ICS DTSTART falls in 2019-2023 (345 rows in 2022, 0 rows in 2024/2025/2026 at review time), despite the CKAN package metadata itself claiming a daily update frequency. This is a dead/abandoned feed, not a live one — per this task's brief, not implemented on that basis.
entries.rights_notes: Explicit CC-Zero (public domain) licence stated on the CKAN dataset package itself — the clearest rights status found anywhere in this research session. Recorded GREEN despite UNSUITABLE_AUTOMATION monitoring status because rights and technical suitability are independent axes (docs/SOURCE_REGISTRY.md); this dataset would be immediately usable rights-wise if the municipality ever resumes publishing current data into it.
entries.research_notes: A genuinely valuable technical/rights finding despite being unusable tonight: if Porto's open-data team ever resumes populating this feed, it would immediately outrank every other Porto source researched here on both licence clarity and structure (it even carries latitude/longitude directly).

research_provenance.note: DISCOVERED rather than TECHNICALLY_REVIEWED: the acquisition path itself works, but the underlying data is dead, so no Observation pipeline was built against it.

entries.name: Câmara Municipal de Vila Nova de Gaia — Eventos / Gaia Cultura
entries.acquisition_path_detail: PORTO-COVERAGE-02: proven live. The 2026-08-24 /rss-feed 404 finding still holds (confirmed, different CMS to Odivelas), but the municipality's own public /pt/eventos/ page (and its own bounded pagination, /pt/eventos/pagina-N/ — exactly 2 real pages at review time) server-renders a genuine, multi-category events listing: one <li> per item inside <ul class="blocoEventosList -events">, each carrying the site's own first-party category tag (e.g. '# música', '# desporto', '# infância'), a free-text date field (single day, same-month day-list/range, cross-month range, or cross-month-and-year range — every real shape retained and parsed honestly, never guessed — see ingestion/cm-gaia-eventos/observation-adapter.mjs), a title, a short description, and a permalink slug used as source_record_id. A dedicated server-side music-filtered URL (/pt/search.php?q=música&Tags=19) was found referenced by every item's own tag link but returns HTTP 403 to a plain client, so filtering is instead applied to the already-parsed record set using the item's own tag text (still fully source-provided and deterministic, never inferred) — see ingestion/cm-gaia-eventos/discovery.mjs's filterMusicRecords(). No venue/location field is exposed anywhere in this listing or on a sampled event detail page, so every Observation resolves UNRESOLVED (matching the existing cm-odivelas-agenda-cultura precedent) — no venue-specific resolver code was added for this source.
entries.rights_notes: No explicit first-party reuse licence or terms-of-use text was found within this bounded technical proof; not upgraded to GREEN/AMBER on the strength of public accessibility alone, and not downgraded to RED without an explicit evidenced prohibition (docs/DATA_RIGHTS.md). Technical proof does not review or clear rights.
entries.overlap_notes: Also operates a dedicated Auditório Municipal de Gaia and separate 'Gaia Cultura' branded site (gaiacultura.pt); the Arrábida Music / 32º Festival Internacional de Música de Gaia entries observed live are themselves cross-listed on agendaculturalporto.org.
entries.research_notes: General municipal 'Eventos e Destaques' feed (desporto, música, infância, literatura, exposições, artes, formação, cinema, cultura all observed live in the same listing) — this task's own 'do not bulk-import unrelated categories' rule is met by filtering on the item's own tag text, not by narrowing the source itself. entries.name: Câmara Municipal de Matosinhos — Agenda Cultural da AMP
entries.acquisition_path_detail: This municipality runs the same underlying CMS platform as cm-odivelas.pt (identical '/pages/{id}.rss' convention directly confirmed live: GET /pages/325.rss returns a genuine application/rss+xml response). However the specific feed found at that id, 'Eventos do dia' ('Events of the day'), is scoped to only the current day and returned 0 items at check time — not a usable broad future-events feed. The '/rss-feed' directory page Odivelas uses to list its own named feeds returned HTTP 404 here, so the id of a broader (non day-scoped) feed, if one exists on this platform, was not located within this bounded search.

entries.name: Câmara Municipal de Gondomar — Agenda
entries.acquisition_path_detail: PORTO-COVERAGE-02 (2026-08-24) directly fetched /agenda/ live: it is genuinely server-rendered (a WordPress site, not a client-rendered SPA) and exposes a real, structured 'events-box' listing of 60+ items, each carrying a source-provided image, title, permalink, and a free-text date field — but that date field states only a DAY and an unabbreviated MONTH NAME ('20 Setembro'), never a year, anywhere on the listing or on a sampled per-event detail page (no schema.org/JSON-LD, no <time datetime>, no article:published_time). A candidate 'infer the year from the WordPress /wp-content/uploads/YYYY/MM/ upload-date path or the poster image filename' heuristic was tested and rejected: only 6 of 11 sampled poster filenames embed a plausible date token at all, and none of it is guaranteed to be the actual event date rather than an upload/branding artefact — exactly the kind of brittle, non-deterministic inference this task prohibits.
